title: pvLinearExtrusion
body:
## pvLinearExtrusion

Sweeps a polygonal dataset along one vector, creating side faces from its edges and, with Capping, copies of the polygons at both ends; output is polydata. Use it to turn a 2-D outline or planar surface into a prism-like solid surface, e.g. a profile into a constant-thickness part. Use pvLinearCellExtrusion for per-cell heights or volume cells.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The result is a surface, not a volume mesh; mesh it separately if volume cells are needed.
- Capping a closed surface duplicates it rather than building a solid; turning Capping off for a closed surface gives no output.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `LinearExtrusion`. Identity: `filters/LinearExtrusionFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Linear Extrusion filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Capping` | The value of this property indicates whether to cap the ends of the swept surface. Capping works by placing a copy of the input dataset on either end of the swept surface, so it behaves properly if the input is a 2D surface composed of filled polygons. If the input dataset is a closed solid (e.g., a sphere), then if capping is on (i.e., this property is set to 1), two copies of the data set will be displayed on output (the second translated from the first one along the specified vector). If instead capping is off (i.e., this property is set to 0), then an input closed solid will produce no output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PieceInvariant` | The value of this property determines whether the output will be the same regardless of the number of processors used to compute the result. The difference is whether there are internal polygonal faces on the processor boundaries. A value of 1 will keep the results the same; a value of 0 will allow internal faces on processor boundaries. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ScaleFactor` | The value of this property determines the distance along the vector the dataset will be translated. (A scale factor of 0.5 will move the dataset half the length of the vector, and a scale factor of 2 will move it twice the vector's length.) | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Vector` | The value of this property indicates the X, Y, and Z components of the vector along which to sweep the input dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json

  "id": "result",

  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
